correctness.rationale: The genus-four canonical-ruling correspondence separates degree-three from degree-four gonality, and the genus-four effective-degree-two divisor criterion separates degree-four from degree-five nonsplit curves. Parsing all 620 aligned primary Weil groups yields hyperelliptic/cone/split/nonsplit counts 264/274/252/254; the only nonsplit no-base-or-quadratic-point class contributes gonality five. The 620-group certificate verifier recomputes the eight bins and sums to 1044 abstract curves. An independent exact binary-field point enumerator over degrees 1–4 checks a genus-four hyperelliptic, cone and nonsplit triple witness has identical zeta numerator. Reliance on source census completeness and lack of an independent source smoothness proof for the witnesses are explicitly bounded.

value.rationale: Faber–Grantham–Howe formulate the natural problem of whether the zeta function determines ground-field gonality. Beyond the already known yes/no counterexamples, the exact answer 178 mixed Weil groups out of 620 and 21 groups supporting three gonalities quantifies this failure throughout the complete smallest-field genus-four moduli set. The exact eight-bin distribution and explicit triple witness are a useful arithmetic invariant for gonality, Jacobian isogeny and canonical-quadric geometry; no downstream theorem is required.
